newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian balance sheets below Europe standard - study.
newsitem.headline: Italian balance sheets below Europe standard - study.

text.p: Among companies quoted on the Milan stock exchange only about nine percent of Italian firms' balance sheets are in line with the standards of clarity and accessibility of those of listed foreign firms, a study showed.
The report, by Milan consultancy firm Massmedia Partners, applied 26 parameters of clarity and access to key data to the balance sheets of 197 companies of the total 222 listed on the Milan Bourse.
Foreign companies quoted here had the most "accessible" balance sheets, with Eridania Begin-Say leading the field, the study said.
On a sector basis, Italian companies with the best balance sheets were chemical and telecoms groups while the worst were to be found in banks and property companies.

The average mark given to the analysed balance sheets was 43.5 out of 100 which the report described as insufficient. Foreign firms' got a score of 69.5 but only 18 Italian companies obtained at least 70 out of 100.
Massmedia noted that among the Italian companies getting the best marks were those firms more oriented towards markets abroad.
Some of the Italian firms getting good marks for their balance sheets by sector were ENI, Telecom Italia, Pirelli, and Bulgari.
